name: Alabama
summary: Banking Department distinguishes mortgage brokering/processing/underwriting/lead generation from mortgage lending authority and announced a September–December 2026 NMLS transition.

name: Alaska
summary: Division licenses broker-lenders and MLOs. Its guidance flags loans below $25,000 for usury review and possible additional Small Loan Act licensing.

name: Arizona
summary: A.R.S. 6-903 distinguishes residential mortgage broker authority from commercial mortgage broker authority; residential brokering requires the mortgage broker license.

name: Arkansas
summary: Securities Department directs brokers, bankers, servicers and loan officers to the Fair Mortgage Lending Act and jurisdiction-specific NMLS requirements; company, control person, branch and MLO filings are separate.

name: California
summary: DRE mortgage broker compliance manual covers borrower disclosures, trust funds, advertising, advance fees, regulated loans, private money, reporting and covered/higher-priced loans. It is a 2019-revised manual, not a complete current rulebook.

name: Colorado
summary: DORA explicitly repealed rules 5.7 and 5.8 effective September 30, 2025; the formerly required tangible net benefit disclosure form is no longer required under those rules.

name: Connecticut
summary: DOB states mortgage brokers and lenders need Connecticut licensing for consumer-purpose mortgage business; DOB also regulates residential mortgage lead generators.

name: Delaware
summary: Title 5 chapter 21 covers mortgage loan brokers and defines consumer owner-occupied one-to-four family mortgages with transaction or property connections to Delaware.

name: Florida
summary: Section 494.0016 requires covered licensee records, including borrower expense receipts and signed closing statements, for at least three years after original entry; alternate storage may require authorization.

name: Georgia
summary: DBF identifies GRMA, Georgia Fair Lending Act and chapter 80-11 rules. Its FAQ says bona fide discount-point analysis changed to CFPB APOR effective June 1, 2024.

name: Hawaii
summary: DFI FAQ identifies MLO and MLO-company licensing, sponsorship restrictions, manufactured-home coverage and potential licensing of wholesale lending activity.

name: Idaho
summary: DOF describes broker/lender authority for Idaho residential property and independent-contractor processor/underwriter MLO licensing; regular nonmortgage lending can change license selection.

name: Illinois
summary: IDFPR administers the Residential Mortgage License Act and Anti-Predatory Lending Database; it flags private-mortgage exemption certificates in Cook, Kane, Will and Peoria counties.

name: Indiana
summary: Secretary of State regulates loan brokers and branch offices; its definition reaches paid assistance obtaining third-party residential loans even when no loan closes.

name: Iowa
summary: Iowa Code 535B.4 requires licensing for mortgage banker/broker/closing-agent activity and restricts use of banker/broker titles; applications identify principal and branch offices.

name: Kansas
summary: OSBC describes mortgage-company licensing broadly for compensated activity involving Kansas residential property and individual MLO licensing on behalf of a licensed company.

name: Kentucky
summary: KRS 286.8-270 imposes borrower-interest/good-faith duties, material-fact disclosure and accounting for borrower property; broker fees must be disclosed before services.

name: Louisiana
summary: OFI identifies separate covered mortgage broker, lender, MLO and servicing activities under the Louisiana SAFE/RMLA framework.

name: Maine
summary: 9-A section 10-303 requires disclosure before agreement or payment, whichever comes first, covering the bond, escrow treatment of consumer fees and written signed agreement.

name: Maryland
summary: OFR includes brokers within mortgage-lender licensing and publishes net-tangible-benefit, secondary-commercial-loan and electronic/off-site record forms.

name: Massachusetts
summary: Chapter 255E section 2 establishes mortgage broker/lender licensing and conditional exemptions; company exemptions must not be treated as blanket individual MLO exemptions.

name: Michigan
summary: DIFS distinguishes first and secondary mortgage regimes and states a broker-only first-mortgage file is retained three years after closing; closing in one's own name requires lender authority.

name: Minnesota
summary: Chapter 58 governs residential mortgage originators/servicers, including licensing and prohibited conduct; company authority is distinct from individual SAFE licensing.

name: Mississippi
summary: DBCF identifies SAFE Act licensing and links amended April 23, 2026 mortgage regulations, a June 26, 2026 cybersecurity reporting memo and an AI supervisory framework.

name: Missouri
summary: Division states residential brokering, funding, servicing or purchasing requires authority unless exempt; MLO authority is separate and renewal must be approved to remain active.
